output.summary: KEP-279 limits Node self-labeling by kubelets: NodeRestriction admission blocks kubelets from setting labels in the k8s.io and kubernetes.io namespaces except an allowlist, and reserves the node-restriction.kubernetes.io/* prefix for administrators. Status is implemented, stage stable, from 2020-12-22.
output.rationale: Kubelets had total authority over their own Node labels, which made centralized label management hard and let a compromised node escalate privileges. The proposal restricts self-set labels to an allowlist and reserves a prefix for admin-driven node isolation. Per the discussion, the feature was completed in 1.19 after a deprecation/skew period, and the KEP was later marked implemented; the status is given as a fact.

alternatives.option: Keep kubelets free to set arbitrary node labels via --node-labels
alternatives.why_not: The readme states this approach 'greatly compromises security' and makes label management difficult across N kubelet command lines.

alternatives.option: Restrict only the labels and taints via a separate proposal (kubernetes/community#911)
alternatives.why_not: The discussion says work on limiting node control over labels/taints/addresses was planned as a separate proposal; the sources do not say it replaced this KEP.

evidence.quote: Modify the `NodeRestriction` admission plugin to prevent Kubelets from self-setting labels within the `k8s.io` and `kubernetes.io` namespaces
Reserve and document the `node-restriction.kubernetes.io/*` label prefix for cluster administrators that want to label their `Node` objects centrally
Yes, this is completed in 1.19. Relevant PRs: * https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90307
This didn't follow alpha, beta, GA cycle, but basically it's GA now.
We are waiting out a deprecation period for the kubelet, and will finish this out in 1.16
